text: The authors argue that existing debate work overlooks human rationality and judgment, and that judges' prior beliefs have not been considered when evaluating debate's effectiveness, citing Khan et al. [31] among others. They add that no systematic study has examined whether debate guides judges with divergent prior beliefs toward more accurate judgments than single-advisor consultancy.
title: Rahman et al. say Khan et al.'s debate evaluation does not consider judges' prior beliefs
